clue.text: Sovereign remedy for constitutional ills

parts.note: reads like a patent medicine for a weak constitution, but means the royal charter of 1215 that a king was forced to grant to cure the ills of the realm's government

explanation.surface: An advert for a cure-all tonic promising to fix a feeble physique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sovereign remedy' is a stock phrase for an infallible cure, and 'constitutional' suggests health; really the sovereign is King John and the constitution is England's.
explanation.definitionFit: The great charter sealed by King John limited royal power and is seen as a founding cure for England's political grievances.

clue.text: Sailor captures O'Hara round this army position?

indicators.note: the sailor holds the next name inside him, as a captor holds a prisoner

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is the usual crossword sailor
Kim O'Hara is the boy hero of Kipling's novel Kim
a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: A seaman seizes a man called O'Hara and asks about a military posture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Army' is a pun: not military but 'to do with arms', since arms akimbo means hands on hips with elbows out.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing with hands on hips and elbows bent outward is a pose of the arms, hence an 'arm-y' stance.

clue.text: Crazy type brood -of this bird

parts.note: a nut is a crazy person
a hatch is a brood of young birds just out of the egg

explanation.surface: A mad sort of bird's clutch of chicks.
explanation.definitionFit: A small tree-climbing songbird that wedges nuts into bark to crack them.

clue.text: So wild a dance makes band-leader cry "action"!

indicators.note: the letters dance about, jumbling into a fresh order
the leader of a band is its first letter

explanation.surface: A frantic dance has the bandleader shouting the film director's cue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dance' looks like a noun after 'a', but it is the anagram signal on B (first letter of 'band'), CRY and ACTION.
explanation.definitionFit: The Corybantes were frenzied priests of Cybele, so their adjective means frenetically unrestrained.

clue.text: Priest's address girl's taken from the phone book …

indicators.note: the girl's name is removed from the longer word

parts.note: a telephone directory lists addresses and numbers
Di is a short girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone has removed a woman's listing from the telephone book to find a vicar's home.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectory is the house provided for a parish rector, so it is where that clergyman lives.

clue.text: … a turn-up for him, we have to state

indicators.note: a down clue turned up reads from bottom to top, so the word is reversed

parts.note: follows on from the previous clue: him is the priest, the Reverend, abbreviated REV

explanation.surface: Continuing the last clue: a surprise for the vicar, which we must declare.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 5 down: 'him' is the priest there, REV, turned up to VER after A.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to assert or declare something as true.

clue.text: Dramatist takes in wood that burns quickly

indicators.note: the playwright's name swallows the timber word

parts.note: Oscar Wilde, the playwright
fir is a softwood timber

explanation.surface: A playwright gathers kindling that flares fast.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire spreading fast and out of control is the type of anything that blazes rapidly.

clue.text: Boy's overweight to dance

parts.note: Charles is a boy's name; the 's is a link
a ton is a huge weight, so being a ton is being too heavy

explanation.surface: A lad is too fat to go dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively 1920s jazz-age ballroom step named after a city in South Carolina.

clue.text: One meeting a Boojum "will softly and suddenly — away"

definitions.text: One meeting a Boojum "will softly and suddenly — away"

parts.words: One meeting a Boojum "will softly and suddenly — away"
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank from Lewis Carroll's The Hunting of the Snark, where the hunter who meets a Boojum disappears without trace

explanation.surface: A quotation from a nonsense poem with one word left out.
explanation.walkthrough: In Carroll's poem, if the Snark proves to be a Boojum, the finder will 'softly and suddenly' disappear; the missing word completes the line.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing verb means to disappear, which is the Baker's fate at the poem's end.

clue.text: Its choir could be redolent of times past

indicators.note: the letters could be rearranged into a different word

explanation.surface: A church choir with an old-fashioned air.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with a past-era feel belongs to or recalls history.

clue.text: Hill in which the mountain nymph finds Escamillo

indicators.note: the hill word has the nymph placed inside it

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor in England
an oread is a nymph of the mountains in Greek myth

explanation.surface: A nymph on a hilltop comes across a man with a Spanish name.
explanation.walkthrough: OREAD goes inside TOR after its T. Escamillo is the bullfighter in Bizet's opera Carmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Escamillo, Carmen's lover in Bizet's opera, is a bullfighter, so he is an example of the type.

clue.text: Egyptian to choose to follow Christian leader

indicators.note: the choosing word comes after the leader letter
the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to opt is to choose

explanation.surface: An Egyptian decides to become a disciple of a church leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Copts are Egyptian Christians, descendants of the native people of ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Giraffe — a beastly old hybrid?

explanation.surface: A giraffe described as a monstrous ancient crossbreed.
explanation.walkthrough: The old name was coined because the animal seemed to be part camel, part leopard: a hybrid of beasts.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for the long-necked African animal, and literally a camel crossed with a leopard.

clue.text: Circulation booster from a doctor way back in the East

indicators.note: the road word is written backwards

parts.note: a lane is a narrow way or road
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A tonic for the blood supplied by a physician in the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: The adrenal hormone raises heart rate and blood pressure, so it boosts the flow of blood.

clue.text: The case of Brutus for instance

definitions.text: The case of Brutus for instance

parts.words: The case of Brutus for instance
parts.note: sounds like a legal or Shakespearean case concerning Caesar's assassin, but means the grammatical case of a Latin name as subject of a sentence

explanation.surface: A lawyer cites the matter of Caesar's killer as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' is grammatical: Brutus is the Latin subject form of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: In Latin grammar the subject of a verb takes the naming case, and Brutus is that form of the name.

clue.text: In the club we find the new-style weapon

indicators.note: the rearranged word sits in the club

parts.note: a mace is a heavy war club

indicators.note: the second 'the' is given a new style, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Inside the club a modern kind of weapon is to be found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new-style' rearranges the second 'the' into HET, which goes inside MACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad heavy blade used for cutting through vegetation and also as an arm.

clue.text: Turns over measures of capital development

explanation.surface: Something flips over while capital growth is gauged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' means the head: hat sizes measure how big a head has grown.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat that overturns keels over; and the measurements of headgear gauge how large a head is.

clue.text: Admission of dishonesty one put in, describing one's surroundings

indicators.note: the single letter is inserted into the confession

parts.note: saying 'am bent' admits to being crooked, bent meaning corrupt
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A confession of crookedness has someone describing their environment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' is slang for corrupt; I goes into AM BENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambient describes the environment or atmosphere around a person.

clue.text: Current is so uncertain

explanation.surface: A rumour that is going around remains unsure.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion floating about is widely felt and current; plans still undecided are unsettled.

clue.text: Bird's Medley in A Flat

indicators.note: a medley is a mixture, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A bird sings a medley of tunes in A flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A Flat' looks like a musical key, but A and FLAT join IN as letters to be mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigeon breed with a spread fan-shaped tail, also the name of a flycatcher.

clue.text: Irish housewife's aide makes us reel with a punch

indicators.note: the letters are made into something new, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: An Irish domestic helper hits us so hard we stagger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes us reel' sounds like a stunning blow, but REEL, A and PUNCH are the letters rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Irish folklore's little fairy cobbler was said to do household tasks at night.

clue.text: Beat includes river water in the Highlands

indicators.note: the beating word holds the letter inside

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A thrashing includes a stream of Highland water.
explanation.definitionFit: A small mountain lake, a word used in northern Britain.

clue.text: Heat rising before end of fall of the rain, say

indicators.note: the turned word comes ahead of the final letter
in a down clue rising means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: anger is heat of temper

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Warmth rises before the end of a rainy downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reverses ANGER to REGNA; 'say' warns that 'rain' stands for its sound-alike, reign.
explanation.definitionFit: Regnal means relating to a monarch's period on the throne, which 'rain' sounds like.

clue.text: Painfully sharp point damaged nag internally

indicators.note: the rearranged horse goes inside the point word
the letters of the horse are damaged, so mixed up

explanation.surface: A sharp spike has injured an old horse inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' turns NAG into GNA, put inside POINT.
explanation.definitionFit: Poignant once meant piercing and now means keenly distressing to the feelings.

clue.text: Eager to behead the old giant

indicators.note: the first letter is cut off

parts.note: Magog is one of the legendary giants Gog and Magog of old British lore

explanation.surface: Keen to decapitate an ancient giant.
explanation.definitionFit: Agog means excitedly keen and expectant.

clue.text: Rural deity In a Roman road? That's for the birds!

indicators.note: the rural god is placed in the road phrase

parts.note: via is Latin for road, as in the Via Appia
a faun is a Roman rustic god, half man half goat

explanation.surface: A country god on an ancient Roman road, dismissed as a matter for the birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's for the birds' is slang for worthless, but here it is literal: FAUN goes in A VIA.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird life of a region taken together is its feathered population.

clue.text: Ring. Free choice? Not entirely

indicators.note: only part of the phrase is used, the letters lying inside it

explanation.surface: A call that offers a free choice, but not completely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a phone call; it means resound again.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring is to resound, sending a sound back once more.

clue.text: Guiding principle of Midas's reign?

explanation.surface: A rule of conduct for a king whose touch made gold.
explanation.walkthrough: King Midas turned all he touched to gold, so his reign was a gilded one.
explanation.definitionFit: The maxim 'do as you would be done by' is a guiding precept; and Midas's kingship was a gilded government.
